judged_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse switches to the stripping minimum schema whenever the sharing env flags are set, but Salesforce's refresh never goes through the sync endpoint — it always parses Salesforce's real response — so the persisted key keeps only {access_token, refresh_token} and loses instance_url, signature, scope and token_type. With sharing enabled, the first Salesforce operation corrupts the stored credential (instance_url gone), and the next jsforce.Connection is constructed without an instance URL, so every subsequent Salesforce operation fails until the user re-authenticates.

adjudication.rationale: In `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, the decision to use `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is based only on `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, not on whether the refresh actually went through the sync endpoint. Salesforce’s refresh path in `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts` always calls Salesforce directly and then calls `parseRefreshTokenResponse(accessTokenJson, salesforceTokenSchema)`, so with those env vars set it will parse with the minimum schema instead of `salesforceTokenSchema`. That can cause either (a) parse failure (minimum schema appears to require at least one numeric property, which Salesforce token responses don’t obviously include) and throw, or (b) if it did succeed, zod would strip fields not declared in the minimum schema, risking loss of required Salesforce fields (eg `instance_url`) when persisting the credential. Either way, the env-driven schema switch introduces broken behavior for non-synced refresh flows like Salesforce.
